title: Auto Loans: Late Charge Assessment
content:
A late charge on an Auto Loans account is assessed per installment, under the terms of the state in which the borrower lives.

## Rule

- **Governing state.** The late charge follows the borrower's home state as the customer profile records it on the day the installment falls due.
- **When it applies.** An installment that remains unsatisfied throughout the state's grace period incurs a late charge. The grace period is counted in calendar days, starting with the day that follows the installment's due date. The charge applies once today's date lies beyond the due date extended by the state's grace days, provided the installment was still unsatisfied when that final grace day ended. The last grace day itself does not qualify.
- **Amount.** The charge is the state's late charge percentage of the monthly payment, taken to the nearest cent with halves going up, and then held to the state's dollar limit per installment; the smaller of the rounded percentage figure and that limit is the charge.
- **How it is recorded.** It is booked as a late charge carrying that installment's due date, dated the first day after the grace period.
- **One per installment.** No installment ever carries more than one late charge; an existing late charge on the same installment is identified from the loan's activity.
- **Where no late charge applies.** An installment deferred by an extension, the fee share of a payment, and any loan whose status has become charged off or paid off never attract a late charge.
- **Collection.** Late charges join the loan's fees due and are taken first out of later payments.

## Grace boundary (abstract and hypothetical dates)

For an installment due on day D in a state whose grace period is G days, day D plus G is the last grace day; a late charge can arise from day D plus G plus one onward, and only if the installment was still unsatisfied at the close of day D plus G. Taking, purely for illustration, a grace period of 12 days and a due date of 10 May: 22 May is the last grace day, a payment satisfying the installment on 22 May prevents the charge, and 23 May is the first day on which a charge dated 23 May can apply.

## Amount examples (invented rate and limit)

With a hypothetical rate of 4.5 percent and a hypothetical limit of 20.00 dollars: an installment of 437.50 gives 19.6875, rounded to 19.69, which is under the limit, so the charge is 19.69; an installment of 520.00 gives 23.40, above the limit, so the charge is 20.00.
